questions.title: Medical history
questions.text: Steroids are thought to create male pattern hair loss by causing your body to produce higher levels of dihydrotestosterone (DHT). DHT acts on the hair follicles on your scalp, causing them to weaken over time. They eventually die and stop growing back, which results in baldness. Taking Finasteride or Propecia is unlikely to be helpful if you are still taking steroids. Steroids can also cause lots of other problems such as erectile dysfunction, infertility, heart and kidney problems as well as mood disorders.

questions.title: Finasteride and trying for a baby
questions.text: Finasteride can affect sperm quality in some men, which may make it harder to conceive. This is uncommon and sperm quality usually improves after stopping treatment . Only small amounts of finasteride pass into semen. Harm to a baby through this exposure is considered very unlikely. As a precaution, we don't prescribe finasteride to men who are trying for a baby. If you are planning to try for a baby, we recommend stopping finasteride at least 3 months before trying to conceive.

questions.title: Living with Pets
questions.text: You've told us that you live with pets. Some of our treatments contain topical minoxidil , which is toxic to all pets including cats and dogs . The main risk is accidental exposure, for example if a pet licks minoxidil from your fingers, hair, skin, clothing, or bedding after application. Oral tablets or capsules are less likely to pose a risk because the medication does not sit on your hair or skin in the same way. However, tablets or capsules are still harmful if a pet ingests them. By continuing, you confirm that you understand this risk and will take appropriate precautions to protect your pets.
